channel.title: The Colorado Sun - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Colorado Sun (coloradosun.com)

item.title: Colorado now has 6 million people, even amid slowing population growth
item.description: But the state saw more folks move out of state than move in. The State Demography Office attributes the declines in net migration to migrants who left.

item.title: “What’d I Miss?”: A different kind of struggle with identity
item.description: In "What'd I Miss?" Ossie confides with Myra about his conflicting feelings about respecting a person's identity in spite of their personality.

item.title: Jim Morrissey: Washing down anti-Colorado vengeance
item.description: Cartoonist Jim Morrissey weighs in on the motives — and impact — behind Trump’s veto of a funding bill for the Arkansas Valley Conduit.

item.title: Drew Litton: The voice(s) of the fans
item.description: Cartoonist Drew Litton depicts the offseason tribulations of Denver football fans as they weigh regular-season success against playoff failure.

item.title: Report: Colorado needs additional $50M annually for water projects, and severance taxes aren’t the answer
item.description: State task force is examining new funding options, including the potential for new taxes or a long-term trust fund to fill the cash gap

item.title: Colorado answers Trump administration’s demand for information about wolf reintroduction, pushes back on malfeasance accusations
item.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife had until Jan. 18 to give the Fish and Wildlife a complete accounting of its wolf management actions since reintroduction started in 2023. They did. Now the ball is in the director’s court.

item.title: Did a Douglas County official claim the Chinese Communist Party funded opposition to home rule?
item.description: Yes. Douglas County Commissioner George Teal claimed the Chinese Communist Party bankrolled opposition to a 2025 home rule measure.

item.title: Tri-State says no thanks to federal orders to keep Craig coal power plant open
item.description: The co-op and one of its partners formally object, saying being forced to keep Craig 1 running upsets the ability to deliver clean power from a new, nearby solar farm

item.title: State regulators get an earful on Xcel power shutdowns from Coloradans left without electricity for days
item.description: State utilities regulators collected testimony from 4,000 businesses, households with lifesaving medical equipment and the merely annoyed as they form rules for public safety power shut-offs

item.title: Avian flu hits another Weld County egg farm, Colorado declares disaster
item.description: First commercial chicken outbreak since 2024 has health, ag authorities on alert again
